questions.question: What does an image histogram primarily show?
In the histogram shown, what do the horizontal and vertical axes represent?
For the small image example, which intensity occurs three times?
Which information cannot be obtained from an image histogram alone?
Can an image be uniquely reconstructed using only its histogram?
options: No, different images can share the same histogram
Yes, if the histogram is normalized
Only when the image is square

questions.question: What is the sum of all values in a normalized histogram?
An 8×8 image has three pixels at intensity 0. What is P(r₀)?
Which statement best defines image brightness?
options: The number of colours in the image
The overall lightness or darkness of the image
The difference between maximum and minimum dimensions

questions.question: What does image contrast describe?
options: The difference in brightness between objects or regions

questions.question: Based on the examples, which scene has higher contrast?
In the brightness sequence, what changes most directly from left to right?
A histogram concentrated within a small intensity range usually indicates what?
Which histogram pattern is most consistent with an underexposed image?
options: Values crowded toward the dark end
Values evenly spread across the range
A single peak at mid-grey only
Values crowded toward the bright end

questions.question: In an 8-bit image, highlight saturation occurs when many pixels are clipped near which value?
For K possible intensity levels, a full-contrast image ideally spans which range?
How is luminance commonly estimated when converting RGB to grayscale?
options: By keeping only the red channel
By a weighted sum of R, G and B

questions.question: What can separate R, G and B component histograms reveal particularly well?
options: The exact position of every colour

questions.question: Why may saturation in individual RGB channels be unclear in the luminance histogram?
options: Channel effects are combined into one weighted value

questions.question: If hR(50), hG(50), and hB(50) each equal 100, what can be concluded about pixels with RGB=(50,50,50)?
options: At most 100 such pixels may exist

questions.question: What is the main purpose of histogram equalization?
options: To convert every image to colour
To improve contrast by redistributing intensities

questions.question: Which function is central to the intensity mapping used in histogram equalization?
How many pixels are present in the 4×4 example image?
Which histogram matches the 4×4 example in the slides?
How is a normalized histogram value p(rₖ) calculated?
Which statement about a valid CDF is correct?
options: It never decreases and ends at 1
It must decrease at every level
It sums to the number of pixels

questions.question: Why is the basic histogram-equalization result normally rounded?
options: To force the histogram to be uniform
Because output intensity levels must be integers
To preserve the original histogram exactly

questions.question: What is the purpose of CDF-min normalization?
options: To map the first occupied intensity to zero
To make every bin contain the same count
To convert RGB directly to HSV

questions.question: Does histogram equalization guarantee an exactly uniform histogram?
options: No, especially for small images with discrete intensities
Only when no CDF is used

questions.question: What is a possible undesirable effect of histogram equalization on a very narrow histogram?
Why does histogram equalization have little effect on the fourth example?
options: Its intensities already span almost the full scale
Its histogram has only one bin

questions.question: What is the main purpose of spatial filtering in image analysis?
options: To change the image file format
To modify pixels using neighbouring values for enhancement or analysis
To convert every image into binary form

questions.question: What distinguishes a linear spatial filter from a non-linear filter?
options: A linear output is a weighted sum of neighbouring pixels

questions.question: What happens as a kernel moves across an image?
options: Neighbouring pixels are multiplied by kernel coefficients and summed
Every pixel is replaced by the image maximum
Only the border pixels are processed

questions.question: What is the operation of applying a kernel over an image commonly called?
What does a mean filter use as the new centre-pixel value?
options: The arithmetic average of the neighbourhood

questions.question: How many pixel values contribute to a 3×3 mean-filter output?
What happens when the mean-filter size increases from 3×3 to 15×15?
options: The image gains more colour channels

questions.question: What happens to isolated salt-and-pepper noise after a linear box filter?
options: Noise peaks are flattened but may remain

questions.question: How should a mean filter process an RGB image?
options: Apply the filter separately to the red, green, and blue channels
Convert the image to binary first
Average the channel names rather than their pixels

questions.question: Which is a main disadvantage of the mean filter?
options: It blurs edges and removes fine detail

questions.question: How does a Gaussian filter weight pixels in its neighbourhood?
options: Corner pixels receive the highest weight
Only the centre pixel receives a weight
The centre receives the largest weight and weights decrease with distance

questions.question: What does the Gaussian parameter σ mainly control?
options: The spread of the kernel and amount of smoothing

questions.question: After normalising a Gaussian kernel, what should its coefficients sum to?
Which factor normalises the common 3×3 integer Gaussian approximation?
Compared with an equal-weight mean filter, what often characterises Gaussian smoothing?
options: It selects the middle ranked value
It produces a smoother, more natural-looking blur

questions.question: What type of derivative does the Laplacian filter approximate?
How does the Laplacian respond in a constant-intensity region?
options: It produces a response close to zero
It produces the maximum possible value

questions.question: Why do Laplacian kernel coefficients normally sum to zero?
options: To ensure all outputs are positive
To give no response in a constant region

questions.question: What changes when the sign of a Laplacian kernel is reversed?
options: The response sign changes, but detected edge locations remain
The kernel becomes a median filter
The filter can no longer sharpen

questions.question: Which limitation is associated with Laplacian filtering?
options: It is highly sensitive to noise
It always preserves the original range

questions.question: What does the Sobel filter estimate?
options: The first derivative or image gradient

questions.question: Which expression gives the Sobel gradient magnitude from Gx and Gy?
Which quantity describes the direction of the image gradient?
options: The gradient orientation, often computed from Gy and Gx

questions.question: How does a median filter determine the output pixel?
options: It sorts the neighbourhood values and selects the middle one

questions.question: In the median-filter example, which value replaces the noisy pixel 255?
questions.note: This is more like pointing to a specific example in the lesson. Therefore, these kind of questions are not expected.

questions.question: Which filter is generally most effective for removing salt-and-pepper noise while preserving edges?
For the shown 3×3 neighbourhood, what output does the maximum filter produce?
Which effect is expected from a maximum filter?
options: It can remove dark pepper noise and expand bright regions
It smooths Gaussian noise using weighted averages

questions.question: For the shown 3×3 neighbourhood, what output does the minimum filter produce?
Which classification of the filters is correct?
options: Mean, Gaussian, Laplacian, and Sobel are linear; median, maximum, and minimum are non-linear
Only the mean filter is linear
Sobel and Laplacian are non-linear rank filters
Median, maximum, and minimum are linear convolution filters
